extracted.intended_audience: trainers and participants of mathematical contests (high school and undergraduate levels); high school teachers running math clubs; individuals preparing for IMO, Tournament of the Towns, Putnam non-calculus
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher product page describing a problem-solving training book aimed at contest trainers and participants; summarizes scope, chapter structure, topics covered, and solution completeness for preparing students for contests up to IMO and noncalculus Putnam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and competition levels
rubrics_metrics.description: It is written for trainers and participants of contests of all levels up to the highest level: IMO, Tournament of the Towns, and the noncalculus parts of the Putnam Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also appeals to high school teachers conducting a mathematics club who need a range of simple to complex problems; useful for instructors wishing to pose 'problem of the week', 'problem of the month', and 'research problem of the year' to their students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter structure: examples then problems then solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each chapter starts with typical examples illustrating the central concepts, followed by a number of carefully selected problems and their solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers interested in increasing the effectiveness of the book can do so by working on the examples in addition to the problems thereby increasing the number of problems to over 1300.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution completeness and hints
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the solutions are complete, but some merely point to the road leading to the final solution. Very few problems have no solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should expect a mix of full solutions and hint-style guidance; instructors may use partially-solved items as starting points for classroom exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of problem sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of competition problems from over twenty major national and international mathematical competitions for high school students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a wide array of interesting, challenging problems drawn from many established contest sources — suitable for varied difficulty levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended pedagogical uses
rubrics_metrics.description: A must-have for instructors wishing to enrich their teaching with interesting non-routine problems; provides individuals with a wide array of interesting, challenging problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested uses include weekly/monthly problems and longer-term research problems to foster a creative classroom atmosphere and continuous discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core topics and strategies covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of contents lists chapter topics: The Invariance Principle; Coloring Proofs; The Extremal Principle; The Box Principle; Enumerative Combinatorics; Number Theory; Inequalities; The Induction Principle; Sequences; Polynomials; Functional Equations; Geometry; Games; Further Strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topics indicate the strategic and topical scope of the book and can guide instructors/learners when selecting chapters aligned with contest syllabi or training goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and accessibility note
rubrics_metrics.description: PDF accessibility summary: This PDF is not accessible. It is based on scanned pages and does not support features such as screen reader compatibility or descriptions for non-text content (e.g., images and graphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users with accessibility needs may not be able to use this content effectively; contact publisher via accessibility request form for assistance or alternative formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness as a comprehensive training resource
rubrics_metrics.description: This volume is the most complete training book on the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioned as a comprehensive repository (over 1300 exercises if examples are worked), suitable for sustained contest preparation and instructor curriculum design.
